label: def: wasserstein
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def: wasserstein}
For $n \in \mathbb N$ and $r \in [1, \infty)$, define vectors $a^1, \ldots, a^k \in \mathbb R^n$ and a random vector $(A^1, \ldots, A^k) \in \mathbb R^k$, we write \[
(a^1, \ldots, a^k) \stackrel{W_r}{\to} (A^1, \ldots, A^k), n\to \infty,
\]
for the Wasserstein-$r$ convergence of the empirical distribution of the rows of $(a^1, \ldots, a^k) \in \mathbb R^{n\times k}$ to the joint law of $(A^1, \ldots, A^k)$. This means, for any continuous function $\phi: \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ and input vector $(a_i^1, \ldots, a_i^k) \in \mathbb R^k$ satisfying the polynomial growth condition (of order $r$)
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq: polynomial growth}
    |\phi (a_i^1, \ldots, a_i^k)| \leq C (1 + \|(a_i^1, \ldots, a_i^k )\|_2^r)  \mbox{ for a constant } C > 0,
\end{eqnarray}
we have as $n \to \infty$,
\[
\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i =1}^n \phi(a_i^1, \ldots, a_i^k) \to E [\phi (A^1, \ldots, A^k)] .
\]

label: rem: det_vs_empirical
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem: det_vs_empirical}
    In the matrix AMP analysed in \cite{tan2024approximate}, the `Onsager' matrices $\bar{F}^k$ and $\bar{C}^k$ in \eqref{eq: CF limiting} are defined via empirical averages rather than expectations. Lemma \ref{lem: wasserstein convergence of matrix AMP} holds for the matrix AMP iteration \eqref{eq: generic AMP algorithm} with either empirical or deterministic versions of $\bar{F}^k, \bar{C}^k$. In fact, the proof of \cite[Theorem 3.4]{tan2024approximate} is based on a reduction to an abstract AMP iteration analysed by \cite{wang2024universality}, which uses deterministic Onsager coefficients.

label: lem: inliers near AMP iterate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: inliers near AMP iterate}  Consider the setting of Lemma \ref{lem: vanishing increments}.
        For $a \in (0, \infty)$ and $\eta \in (0, a/2)$, let $q_* (\eta) =  \mathbb P\left( |Z_1 + \sigma(Z_2)\bar\varepsilon - Z_1^* | < (a - 2\eta)(1 + b_*) \right)$, then it holds that $\lim_{\eta \to 0}  q_*(\eta) =  \delta^{-1} (1 + b_*^{-1})$. Further, define
        $q_k (\eta) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n I\left\{ |Y_i - \tilde X_i^\top \check\beta^{k+1}| < (a - \eta) \right\}$, it holds that 
        \[\mathbb P (\liminf_{k\to\infty}\liminf_{n, p \to\infty} q_k (\eta ) \ge q_*(\eta) ) = 1 . \]
